# Data Source: stripe_financial_connections_account

A bank account that a customer, or the account itself, linked through Financial Connections. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_financial_connections_account" "checking" {
  id = "fca_1MwVK82eZvKYlo2Cjw8FMxXf"
}

output "institution_name" {
  value = data.stripe_financial_connections_account.checking.institution_name
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the financial connections account to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `account_holder` - The account holder that this account belongs to. See [`account_holder`](#account_holder) below.
* `account_numbers` - Details about the account numbers. See [`account_numbers`](#account_numbers) below.
* `balance` - The most recent information about the account's balance. See [`balance`](#balance) below.
* `balance_refresh` - The state of the most recent attempt to refresh the account balance. See [`balance_refresh`](#balance_refresh) below.
* `category` - The type of the account. Account category is further divided in `subcategory`. Possible values: `cash`, `credit`, `investment`, `other`.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `display_name` - A human-readable name that has been assigned to this account, either by the account holder or by the institution.
* `institution_name` - The name of the institution that holds this account.
* `last4` - The last 4 digits of the account number. If present, this will be 4 numeric characters.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `ownership` - The most recent information about the account's owners.
* `ownership_refresh` - The state of the most recent attempt to refresh the account owners. See [`ownership_refresh`](#ownership_refresh) below.
* `permissions` - The list of permissions granted by this account.
* `status` - The status of the link to the account. Possible values: `active`, `disconnected`, `inactive`.
* `status_details` - See [`status_details`](#status_details) below.
* `subcategory` - If `category` is `cash`, one of: - `checking` - `savings` - `other` If `category` is `credit`, one of: - `mortgage` - `line_of_credit` - `credit_card` - `other` If `category` is `investment` or `other`, this will be `other`. Possible values: `checking`, `credit_card`, `line_of_credit`, `mortgage`, `other`, `savings`.
* `subscriptions` - The list of data refresh subscriptions requested on this account.
* `supported_payment_method_types` - The [PaymentMethod type](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object#payment_method_object-type)(s) that can be created from this account.
* `transaction_refresh` - The state of the most recent attempt to refresh the account transactions. See [`transaction_refresh`](#transaction_refresh) below.

<a id="account_holder"></a>
### `account_holder`

The `account_holder` attribute supports:

* `account` - The ID of the Stripe account that this account belongs to. Only available when `account_holder.type` is `account`.
* `customer` - The ID for an Account representing a customer that this account belongs to. Only available when `account_holder.type` is `customer`.
* `customer_account` -
* `type` - Type of account holder that this account belongs to. Possible values: `account`, `customer`.

<a id="account_numbers"></a>
### `account_numbers`

The `account_numbers` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `expected_expiry_date` - When the account number is expected to expire, if applicable.
* `identifier_type` - The type of account number associated with the account. Possible values: `account_number`, `tokenized_account_number`.
* `status` - Whether the account number is currently active and usable for transactions. Possible values: `deactivated`, `expired`, `pending`, `transactable`.
* `supported_networks` - The payment networks that the account number can be used for.

<a id="balance"></a>
### `balance`

The `balance` attribute supports:

* `as_of` - The time that the external institution calculated this balance. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `cash` - See [`balance.cash`](#balance.cash) below.
* `credit` - See [`balance.credit`](#balance.credit) below.
* `current` - The balances owed to (or by) the account holder, before subtracting any outbound pending transactions or adding any inbound pending transactions. Each key is a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Each value is a integer amount. A positive amount indicates money owed to the account holder. A negative amount indicates money owed by the account holder.
* `type` - The `type` of the balance. An additional hash is included on the balance with a name matching this value. Possible values: `cash`, `credit`.

<a id="balance.cash"></a>
### `balance.cash`

The `balance.cash` attribute supports:

* `available` - The funds available to the account holder. Typically this is the current balance after subtracting any outbound pending transactions and adding any inbound pending transactions. Each key is a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Each value is a integer amount. A positive amount indicates money owed to the account holder. A negative amount indicates money owed by the account holder.

<a id="balance.credit"></a>
### `balance.credit`

The `balance.credit` attribute supports:

* `used` - The credit that has been used by the account holder. Each key is a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Each value is a integer amount. A positive amount indicates money owed to the account holder. A negative amount indicates money owed by the account holder.

<a id="balance_refresh"></a>
### `balance_refresh`

The `balance_refresh` attribute supports:

* `last_attempted_at` - The time at which the last refresh attempt was initiated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `next_refresh_available_at` - Time at which the next balance refresh can be initiated. This value will be `null` when `status` is `pending`. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `status` - The status of the last refresh attempt. Possible values: `failed`, `pending`, `succeeded`.

<a id="ownership_refresh"></a>
### `ownership_refresh`

The `ownership_refresh` attribute supports:

* `last_attempted_at` - The time at which the last refresh attempt was initiated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `next_refresh_available_at` - Time at which the next ownership refresh can be initiated. This value will be `null` when `status` is `pending`. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `status` - The status of the last refresh attempt. Possible values: `failed`, `pending`, `succeeded`.

<a id="status_details"></a>
### `status_details`

The `status_details` attribute supports:

* `active` - See [`status_details.active`](#status_details.active) below.

<a id="status_details.active"></a>
### `status_details.active`

The `status_details.active` attribute supports:

* `action` - The action (if any) to proactively relink the Account. Possible values: `none`, `relink_required`.
* `cause` - The underlying cause of the Account becoming inactive. Possible values: `access_expired`, `institution_requirement`, `unspecified`.
* `expected_deactivation_date` - When the Account is expected to become inactive, if applicable.

<a id="transaction_refresh"></a>
### `transaction_refresh`

The `transaction_refresh` attribute supports:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `last_attempted_at` - The time at which the last refresh attempt was initiated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `next_refresh_available_at` - Time at which the next transaction refresh can be initiated. This value will be `null` when `status` is `pending`. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `status` - The status of the last refresh attempt. Possible values: `failed`, `pending`, `succeeded`.
